questions.q: What distinguishes manual sharing from OWD, the role hierarchy, and sharing rules, per this lesson?
options: It's the only mechanism that applies before object permissions are checked
It's the only mechanism that is deliberate and one-off rather than systematic and automatic
It's the only mechanism that can restrict access below OWD
It's the only mechanism that requires a Salesforce Shield license
questions.explain: Every other mechanism in the chapter applies automatically to every matching record; manual sharing is a deliberate, individual action on one record.

questions.q: How does an admin or owner actually perform a manual share?
options: By writing a criteria-based sharing rule
By editing the role hierarchy
Through the record's own Share button, granting access to one specific user or group
By changing the object's organization-wide default
questions.explain: Manual sharing happens directly on the record via its Share button, not through any rule or hierarchy setting.

questions.q: What example does the lesson give for when manual sharing is the right tool, rather than a sharing rule?
options: Sharing every Account with the entire sales team permanently
A recruiter going on vacation temporarily sharing job applications with a covering colleague
Giving every user View All on Opportunity
Restricting a sensitive field from an entire profile
questions.explain: The lesson uses this exact example — too narrow and temporary to justify building a sharing rule, which is what makes manual sharing the right fit.

questions.q: What can happen to a manually-shared record when its owner changes, per this lesson?
options: Nothing -- manual shares always persist regardless of ownership changes
Salesforce may remove manual shares the previous owner granted, since the grant was theirs to give
The record automatically becomes Private to everyone
The new owner is blocked from editing the record for 24 hours
questions.explain: The lesson flags this as a real gotcha: manual shares granted by the previous owner can be removed when ownership transfers.

questions.q: How do Account, Opportunity, and Case Teams (previewed in this lesson) differ from manual sharing?
options: Teams are a one-time grant; manual sharing is a standing structure
They are functionally identical with different names
Teams provide standing, collaborative access re-applied across many records; manual sharing is a one-off grant on a single record
Teams only work for Leads, never Accounts, Opportunities, or Cases
questions.explain: The lesson previews teams as a durable, reusable structure for ongoing collaboration, contrasted with manual sharing's one-time, single-record nature.
